headline: Democrats are focused on affordability. Some say they should focus on democracy too
summary: Democratic candidates have focused on affordability. But some party leaders say they also need to talk about democracy, especially if President Trump continues making unfounded claims about election fraud.

headline: In a day of tributes, Lindsey Graham is remembered as a tireless Washington mainstay
summary: Lawmakers, foreign leaders and President Trump gathered Tuesday for the first of two days of funeral services for the late South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham.

headline: Trump to meet with Ukraine's Zelenskyy and Israel's Netanyahu
summary: President Trump says he will meet with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu Tuesday setting up a big day of foreign policy.

headline: Former Pentagon official on Trump's meetings with the leaders of Ukraine and Israel
summary: NPR's A Martínez asks former senior Pentagon official Evelyn Farkas about President Trump's potential priorities as he meets the leaders of Ukraine and Israel.

headline: Trump shattered ethics norms. Will voters trust Democrats to fix them?
summary: Democrats are making the case that now is the time to tackle anti-corruption reforms — to serve as a check on Donald Trump and to overhaul a system voters say is co-opted against their interests.

headline: Survey finds most Americans believe corruption is a problem in politics
summary: Voters indicate they're increasingly concerned about corruption in public office. A new survey indicates that concern spans the political spectrum.

headline: Rand Paul releases Anthony Fauci's pandemic-era diary notes. Here's what they tell us
summary: Sen. Rand Paul has released a tranche of Dr. Anthony Fauci's diary entries from the COVID-19 pandemic. Fauci is set to appear before a Senate committee Wednesday on the origins of the coronavirus.

headline: Platner energized Maine's Democrats. Jackson's challenge will be to keep them engaged
summary: Democrats have a new candidate for U.S. Senate in Maine: Troy Jackson. In one of the country's most closely-watched races, he'll have less than 100 days to make his case.

headline: Inside Joe Manchin's new quest to elect more Independents to Congress
summary: The former West Virginia senator was a lifelong Democrat before deciding to register as an independent two years ago. He now wants to create similar pathways for other politicians in both parties.

headline: With less than 100 days left until Election Day, how the midterms are shaping up
summary: There are now fewer than 100 days until Election Day in November. Here's how NPR's Mara Liasson sees the midterm campaign shaping up.

headline: Kalshi attacks a Wisconsin law banning election bets as 'voter suppression'
summary: The spat between the leading prediction market company and a key battleground state could be a glimpse into the next major fight between states and the fast-growing industry.

headline: In Memphis, an 'anti-crime' task force quietly turned into an ICE crackdown
summary: The influx of federal agents into the city last fall led to widespread immigration arrests – a majority without criminal convictions. President Trump has said he wants to replicate it elsewhere.

headline: Maine Democrats pick Troy Jackson to replace Graham Platner in Senate race
summary: In Maine's U.S. Senate race, state Democrats have nominated Troy Jackson to replace the scandal-plagued candidate Graham Platner.

headline: With just a few primary elections to go, the competitive Senate map keeps shifting
summary: For Democrats to take control of the U.S. Senate, they have to flip four seats currently held by Republicans. Republicans, meanwhile, are playing defense and pickup opportunities are harder to find.

headline: Troy Jackson replaces Graham Platner as Democratic candidate in Maine's Senate Race
summary: Maine Democrats have chosen their candidate to run against incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins. Troy Jackson, former state lawmaker, steps in where the scandal-plagued Graham Platner stepped out.

headline: Maine Senate Dems Nominee
summary: Maine Democrats have chosen their candidate to run against incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins. Troy Jackson, former state lawmaker, steps in where the scandal-plagued Graham Platner stepped out.

headline: Politics chat: How the war with Iran will shape midterms, Troy Jackson enters Maine Senate race
summary: We'll look at how the war with Iran might shape the outcome for the 2026 Midterm elections, as well as how the new Democratic senate candidate in Maine might fare against the Republican incumbent.

headline: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds
summary: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.

headline: Biden ghostwriter tapes to be released
summary: Former President Joe Biden is declining to appeal a court ruling that allows the Justice Department to publicize recordings of conversations between him and a writer collaborating on his memoir.

headline: Week in Politics: Iran War; Trump attends solemn ritual; nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
summary: The Trump administration is seeking tens of billions of dollars in supplemental appropriations for the Iran War, a war which the president and allies have repeatedly claimed is already won.

headline: Democrats in Maine formally nominate Troy Jackson as their new U.S. Senate candidate
summary: Democrats are hoping to move past Graham Platner's scandal-plagued campaign as they look to unseat Susan Collins. In Jackson, they chose a nominee with a similar economic populist message as Platner.

headline: 'The show must go on.' Trump makes jabs at rescheduled White House Correspondents' dinner
summary: President Trump used his speech to attack his political opponents, members of the media and even members of his own cabinet.

headline: Democrats approve a new primary election calendar, putting South Carolina first
summary: Democrats chose South Carolina for the first 2028 presidential primary, then Nevada, prioritizing Black and Latino voters. New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia also hold early contests.

headline: St. Louis Democratic House primary exposes party rifts over Israel
summary: St. Louis Public Radio hosted one of the first media appearances this year between Rep. Wesley Bell and former Congresswoman Cori Bush. The primary race is a rematch of a race Bush lost last year to Bell.

headline: Trump's replacement tariffs continue to put pressure on U.S. economy
summary: President Trump slapped replacement tariffs on 59 countries and the European Union to replace expiring ones.

headline: Senate advances budget bill after marathon late-night session
summary: Lawmakers voted to advance a compromise spending package early this morning, following weeks of negotiation over a contested infrastructure amendment. A final floor vote is expected by Friday.
